title_candidates: Google opens WeatherNext after a major cyclone-forecasting advance
summary: Google DeepMind open-sourced WeatherNext code and weights after a Nature study found roughly one extra day of useful cyclone forecast lead time.

primary_source.title: WeatherNext: AI model achieves breakthrough in forecasting cyclones
primary_source.author: Google DeepMind
key_facts: WeatherNext predicts cyclone track, intensity, and wind structure together.
The paper reports about one additional day of useful forecast lead time over leading operational models.
The system can produce up to 1,000 possible scenarios extending 15 days ahead.
Google released WeatherNext Cyclones, WeatherNext 2, a smaller model, code, and model weights.
Weather Lab provides experimental visual forecasts and does not replace official warnings.

supporting_sources.title: Operational Tropical Cyclone Forecasting with AI
key_facts: Nature published the paper on August 6, 2026 and reports a day or more of average lead-time advantage.

supporting_sources.title: WeatherNext
key_facts: The public repository includes code, pretrained model information, a Colab notebook, licensing, and experimental-use disclaimers.

prerequisites: A Google account for Weather Lab
Access to your local official weather service

steps.instruction: Inspect one Weather Lab forecast, note its issue time and uncertainty spread, then compare the same place and time with an official weather service.
Use only the official alert for travel, evacuation, school, or safety decisions.

references.title: WeatherNext: AI model achieves breakthrough in forecasting cyclones
references.author: Google DeepMind

references.title: Operational Tropical Cyclone Forecasting with AI
references.author: Ferran Alet and colleagues

risk_flags: WeatherNext and Weather Lab are experimental and must not be presented as replacements for official weather warnings.
The open Colab is a research workflow; the reader guide uses Weather Lab instead of asking general users to run model code.
